c.tagline: La Superba - a maritime maze of palaces, pesto, and the biggest aquarium in Italy.

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are white and metered, with fixed surcharges at night and for luggage. Uber offers only its licensed taxi/black-car service in Genoa (no UberX), so most people hail at a rank or book through Free Now or the itTaxi app.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance; 113 reaches the state police and 118 reaches medical emergencies directly.

avoid.reason: Caution in the old-town alleys (caruggi) near the port at night

hood_desc: One of Europe's largest medieval old towns, a labyrinth of narrow caruggi opening onto Piazza De Ferrari and the striped cathedral; atmospheric and packed with trattorias and focaccia bakeries, though some lanes feel edgy after dark.
The Renaissance 'New Streets' of Via Garibaldi, lined with the UNESCO-listed Palazzi dei Rolli and the Musei di Strada Nuova; the grandest, most elegant slice of the historic centre.

The revitalised old port redesigned by Renzo Piano, home to Italy's largest aquarium, the Galata maritime museum, the Bigo lift, and waterfront restaurants; the most family-friendly, walkable base by the sea.

A refined residential district east of the centre with Liberty-style villas, the seafront Corso Italia promenade, and good restaurants; calm and upmarket, popular with families and longer-stay visitors.
A picture-perfect former fishing hamlet of pastel houses around a tiny pebble cove, famous for gelato and sunset views; quiet and romantic, a short bus or shore walk from the centre.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though some locals prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: The metro runs roughly 5:00 AM to 11:30 PM; buses run from early morning to around midnight with a limited night network, and the Zecca-Righi funicular runs into the evening.
transit.note: Genoa's single metro line plus a dense bus network, two funiculars, and a series of public elevators and lifts help conquer the steep hills; the Genova-Casella narrow-gauge railway climbs into the Apennine foothills.
transit.pay: A single AMT ticket is EUR 1.50 and valid 100 minutes across buses, the metro, funiculars, and public elevators; a day pass is about EUR 4.50. Buy from tobacconists, machines, or the AMT app and validate on boarding; contactless tap-and-go is rolling out.

bus: Autostazione Genova (Piazza della Vittoria, Flixbus & intercity)
ferry: Port of Genoa (Stazione Marittima / Terminal Traghetti)

transit.m: Volabus (line 100) to Piazza Principe & Brignole stations (~30 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a cover charge (coperto) is usually on the bill, so rounding up or leaving a euro or two for good service is appreciated but not expected.
